title: What a loop was briefed with
description: `briefed.json` — the digests of the documents that authorised one `wring run`, captured BEFORE the first worker turn. A SIBLING of the loop bundle's manifest, like `digests.json` and `vacuity.json` and for the same law-7 reason: `wringer.loop.v2`'s manifest is frozen, so this arrives as its own file and a reader that does not know it ignores it. Written before `digests.json`, so the loop's own tamper-evidence covers it. It exists because `deliver.py` wrote `spec_sha256` at three sites and compared it at NONE, and `spec.authorising_sha256` hashes the spec as it is NOW — so a delivery manifest could say 'authorised by spec S' where S was whatever sat on disk at delivery time rather than what the work was briefed against, and `spec.py`'s own docstring named the gap ('a spec could be edited after approval with no trace'). Three documents, because three things authorise a loop's work: the approved spec is the authority everything downstream runs on, the rubric is what 'satisfied' means, and `.wringer.yaml` is what 'verified' means. A mismatch stops the loop at an ITERATION BOUNDARY with reason `authority_moved` — never mid-turn, because a turn that has run cannot be un-run — and refuses delivery with a named reason. Nothing is ever reverted: `deliver.py`'s standing ruling against auto-reversal binds this and binds the wording of the refusal too. ABSENT from every loop bundle written before this file existed, and from every run no loop produced; those deliver exactly as they always have.

schema_version.description: Identifies the record a reader is holding. Versioned independently of the loop bundle (`wringer.loop.v2`) it sits beside.

captured_at.description: Local ISO-8601 with UTC offset, second precision. When the brief was hashed, which is before the first worker turn and after any resume rebuilt the loop.

documents.description: Repo-relative path -> sha256 of its bytes, or null when the document did not exist when the loop was briefed. `null` is a VALUE and not an omission: a spec that appears mid-loop is a move, because the landed work was not briefed against it. A capture that names only some of the documents is a statement about those documents alone and never a claim that the rest were absent.
